newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Helix slides on disappointing drilling.
newsitem.headline: Helix slides on disappointing drilling.

text.p: The shares of gold hopeful, Helix Resources NL fell sharply on Tuesday morning after the company released more drilling results from its Timkillia prospect in the Gawler Craton region of South Australia.
At 11.05 a.m (0005 GMT), Helix shares were A$1.09 weaker at A$3.90 on turnover of 318,442 shares.

"The thing that was making the prospect look economic were the previously reported 100 metre intersections, but if they are now only getting 40 metres or so, the market has looked at it and said it doesn't look so wonderful," a Sydney-based analyst said.
Helix earlier released results from five new holes drilled at the prospect. The best result being a 44 metre intersection at an average of 2.6 grams per tonne (g/t) gold.
The analyst said it was significant that one hole in the sequence found no significant gold intercept.
The latest results have been eagerley awaited by the market after gold producer, Acacia Resources Ltd acquired a 17.4 percent stake in Helix for about A$38 million last week.
Acacia shares fell sharply after the purchase on the perception that the company had paid too much for the stake.
At 11.10 a.m (0010 GMT), Acacia shares were five cents weaker at A$2.14.
